advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that runs with an empty probe_criteria allowlist (normal full review) and overlap=False to confirm _drop_unrequested_overlap removes project.plan-overlap and that routing/coverage reflects it.
evidence: Comment at the probe_criteria line states it narrows the fan-in to the one criterion, so the full-routed path (empty probe allowlist) is never run in the suite
_drop_unrequested_overlap only removes entries that _project_criteria added with an empty allowlist — the path exercised in production full reviews is not covered
advisory.finding: The non-probe (full-review) code path for the overlap off-switch is untested: every test in test_plan_review_overlap.py sets `with_inputs={"overlap": ..., "probe_criteria": [_OVERLAP_ID]}`, so the interaction between normal routing (where project.plan-overlap fans in) and `_drop_unrequested_overlap` is never exercised.
scenarios: A regression where _drop_unrequested_overlap fails to remove the criterion on a full (non-probe) review would not be caught

dropped.finding: The agent-tier drop branch of _drop_unrequested_overlap (newly added line `[c for c in agent if str(c["id"]) != _OVERLAP_ID]`) is never exercised: every off-switch test asserts only the `single` list. test_off_keeps_the_criterion_out_of_batch_resolution checks `off["coverage"]["batch_resolution"]["single"]` but never the agent list, so a regression that stopped dropping the id from the agent fan-in would not be caught.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Pass the `overlap` input to the assemble step (or filter project.plan-overlap out of the assemble routing record when overlap is off) so the coverage/routing record matches what the batch runner actually executes.
evidence: plan-review.yaml assemble step `with:` passes only `ticket_id` and `probe_criteria: ${{ inputs.probe_criteria }}` — no `overlap`
workflow_ops.py:267 `included = {c["id"] for c in single + agent}` includes project.plan-overlap when it routes in (it has no `trigger`, so always applies at container/leaf scope)
workflow_ops.py:274-277 emits routing.single_turn/agent_tier from `included`, and _key emits `include_project_plan-overlap` = True
production_batch_runner.py:125-127 drops the id AFTER routing via `_drop_unrequested_overlap` so execution and the assemble-step coverage record disagree when overlap is off
dropped.finding: The assemble step (`plan_review_assemble_criteria`) is not given the `overlap` input, so on a normal (non-probe) full review with `overlap=False` it records `project.plan-overlap` as included/routed (`include_project_plan-overlap: true`, listed in `routing.single_turn`) even though `_drop_unrequested_overlap` removes it from the batch runner and it never executes — the coverage/routing record misreports a criterion as routed that was silently dropped.
scenarios: A real production review run with overlap=False (the default): routing coverage lists project.plan-overlap but it is never evaluated
An operator reading coverage.routing.single_turn to confirm which criteria ran is misled
dropped.suggested_fix: Thread `overlap: ${{ inputs.overlap }}` into the assemble step's `with:` and have plan_review_assemble_criteria exclude project.plan-overlap from `included`/routing when overlap is false, mirroring _drop_unrequested_overlap.
